cases.title: "The rock" names two layers whose first steps differ: one clarifying question naming both, then an answer that states its assumption

rubric.reason: Turn 1 is a single question naming both layers from the read, 'the shake on rock.png (moved by Shake Control's expressions) or ... the slide on Rock Shadow.png (its own two keys)', with no steps, offer or explanation; the parentheticals only tell the two choices apart.

Turn 2 answers about rock.png without asking again, but it never says what it took the learner to mean: it opens straight with 'In Comp 1, rock.png rides on Shake Control...' and never names its reading of 'heavier'.

checks.detail: no accepted give_answer call in turn 2
explanation of turn 1: never matched /Rock Shadow/

rubric.reason: Turn 1 is one sentence, "do you mean rock.png, which shakes with Shake Control, or Rock Shadow.png, which moves on its own keys?", naming both NAME_PARTIAL candidates from the read; its short clauses only tell the two apart, and it has no steps or offer.
Turn 2 answers on rock.png and Shake Control without asking again, and states once in the first part what it took the learner to mean: "Taking heavier to mean a slower, weightier shake".
